description: Dependency audit — transitive Apache-2.0/GPL-2.0 conflict surfaced before release
scenario: User says: 'We're about to publish the v3 API container image on Docker Hub. Legal wants to know if we're clean — the license file says MIT.' The repo is a Node service with a lockfile, and there is a ./vendor directory with two hand-copied modules.
expected_outcome: Agent inventories from the resolved lockfile and the vendor directory (not from the root LICENSE or package.json), identifies one transitive GPL-2.0-only dependency and one Apache-2.0 dependency that the GPL-2.0-only code links against, states that Apache-2.0 code cannot be combined into a GPL-2.0-only work because GPLv2 §6 forbids additional restrictions, gives concrete remediation options (swap to the GPL-3.0 build, replace the library, or isolate behind a separate process with counsel sign-off), and labels the whole output engineering guidance rather than a legal clearance.
checks: Scans the lockfile and vendored paths, not the declared ranges
Names the specific incompatible pair and the license clause that causes it
Does not declare the project 'compliant' or 'legally safe'
Proposes at least two remediation paths and defers the boundary call to counsel

description: NOTICE generation — aggregates Apache-2.0 notices and full permissive texts, transitively
scenario: User asks: 'Generate the third-party notices file for our desktop app release. We ship about 300 npm packages, 40 of which we list as direct dependencies — 12 of those are Apache-2.0 and the rest are MIT/BSD/ISC.'
expected_outcome: Agent generates the notices from the full resolved tree rather than the 40 direct dependencies, aggregates any upstream NOTICE files verbatim into a NOTICE section (Apache-2.0 §4(d) requires the notices be included and unmodified), emits full license texts for every package rather than URLs, deduplicates by package/version/license while keeping every distinct copyright line, and recommends regenerating in CI with a build failure when the committed file drifts from a fresh generation.
checks: Covers transitive dependencies, not just the declared 40
Preserves upstream NOTICE content verbatim instead of rewriting it
Includes full license texts, not links
Recommends a CI drift check, and mentions SBOM (SPDX/CycloneDX) output

description: CI policy violation — new AGPL dependency blocked with an expiring waiver path
scenario: A pull request adds a document-conversion package that pulls in an AGPL-3.0-only transitive dependency into the server-side bundle. The repo already carries 40 pre-existing copyleft dependencies that predate the policy. The user says: 'The CI gate is failing and it's blocking everyone — can we just switch it to warn?'
expected_outcome: Agent keeps the gate failing and treats the AGPL case as a genuine finding rather than a nuisance: explains that AGPL-3.0 §13 obligates offering corresponding source to users interacting with the software over a network, so a server-side AGPL dependency is exactly the case the gate exists to catch. It baselines the 40 pre-existing dependencies so the gate only fails on new additions, and offers the waiver mechanism with a named owner, a written justification, and an expiry date — not a global downgrade to warn.
checks: Refuses to convert the gate to warn-only
Distinguishes the new AGPL dependency from the baselined historical debt
Explains the §13 network-use obligation in the agent's own words
Waiver, if offered, carries an owner and an expiry
